reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked every English line, with particular attention to the 16 reception-note sites (2:1, 2:10, 3:3, 3:12, 8:3, 11:1, 11:23, 40:2, 40:3, 42:14, 43:2, 44:2, 44:3, 44:15, 44:18, 44:30). No line carries the canon reading: kāḇôḏ stays 'glory' (11:23; 43:2), the bronze man keeps the Hebrew simile (40:3), qōḏeš stays 'holy' against the canon's 'healthful' (42:14), ʾûlām stays 'porch' against the 'airlock' reading (44:3), and yezaʿ is rendered by its accepted sense (44:18). Each reception note was checked against the TBWTT ch. 3 quotation file and is accurate and labelled, except that 11:23 slightly overstates the canon (verdict revise, notes only). Two features a cold reader might query were judged not to be leakage: 'ruach' (an inferred overlay convention that leaves an acknowledged ambiguity open and replaces the ASV's doctrinal capital) and 'between the land and the skies' at 8:3 (the ratified eretz default and shamayim physical register, identical to GEN-WOH 1:1, with the Hebrew's 'in visions of Elohim' kept). The sacrificial and architectural modernizations ('guilt-offering', 'dash', 'guardroom', 'vestibule', 'altar hearth') follow NRSV/NJPS and the lexica and carry no interpretive content.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 207 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 27 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, sources, overlay, central diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-e2-editor-report.md. After reading it no verdict changed. The report raises nothing on 11:19 (a new ruach), 11:23 (reception-note wording) or 44:24 (Ketiv wording in the line), so those stand. Spot-checks the report requested: NRSV 8:16 'temple', 42:1 'temple yard', 42:3 'in three stories', 43:15-16 'altar hearth', Yadin IEJ 8 (1958), the Mesha line-12 ʾrʾl, and Albright 1942 (ziggurat; arallû) are consistent with the reviewer's knowledge; the '43:3 six manuscripts' count and the exact LXX figure at 40:14 could not be confirmed independently and should be checked against BHS or worded as 'some manuscripts' / 'a different figure' (non-blocking). The report's Ketiv/Qere count (48 readings in 24 verses) matches the reviewer's independent count of 50 bracketed tokens.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-quotation-marks: Ratify the Kings convention for Ezekiel. The reviewer's own stack simulation confirms all eight chapters balance and the 43:7-17 boundary is defensible. Schedule a punctuation-only pass on ch. 37 (37:4-5, 9, 12-14, 16, 19, 21-28) and a check of chs. 1 and 10 so the book ships with one convention.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-proper-names: Keep English forms in Ezekiel for this wave: a mixed book would be worse than either practice, and the three signed-off chapters already use English. Recommendation for the corpus decision: the Latter Prophets volumes (isaiah-woh, ezekiel-woh, daniel-woh) already share English forms while genesis/exodus/Kings transliterate; record that genre split explicitly in a central convention note rather than converting Ezekiel, unless the founder wants decision A extended corpus-wide, in which case the mechanical pass over all eleven chapters is straightforward.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-ruach: Ratify the overlay rule for agent/transport rûaḥ, 'spirit' for human idioms and 'side' for the compass sense, and support merging it with the Kings ruach entries into one central entry. Before promotion, narrow the 'gift' clause: rûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ paired with lēḇ (11:19; later 18:31; 36:26a) is the human disposition and should be 'a new spirit', while YHWH's own rûaḥ and the breath of life (36:27; 37:5-6, 14) stay 'ruach'. Verse flag at EZK-WOH-11:19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-inferred-temple-terms: Ship both as inferred. ʾêlām 'vestibule' (NRSV) and harʾēl/ʾăriʾêl 'altar hearth' (NRSV) are lexically supported, replace ASV renderings without lexical basis ('arches', 'upper altar'), and the disputes (40:30 plurals; the 'mountain of El' vocalization) are recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-sacrificial-vocabulary: Ratify the new central entry as direct. 'guilt-offering' and 'dash' are lexically motivated and match NRSV/NJPS and isaiah-woh; Milgrom's alternatives are correctly recorded but not adopted. Add the glossaryRef to EXO-WOH-20:21 and 1KI-WOH-8:63-64 at the next pass of those books.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-refId-prefix: Agree. Normalize EZK- to EZK-WOH- (and GEN- to GEN-WOH-) in one dedicated mechanical central op with a before/after count, separate from any content diff, and only after the Revelation and Ezekiel E2 diffs are both applied.

paragraphs.text: וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל־הַשָּׁ֑עַר שַׁ֕עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פֹּנֶ֖ה דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַקָּדִֽים׃

i18n.en: Then he led me to the gate, the gate that faces toward the east.

notes.official: *haššaʿar ʾăšer pōneh dereḵ haqqāḏîm* 'the gate that faces toward the east': the outer east gate, through which the glory left (10:19; 11:23) and now returns.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֗ה כְּבוֹד֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֖א מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֑ים וְקוֹל֗וֹ כְּקוֹל֙ מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים וְהָאָ֖רֶץ הֵאִ֥ירָה מִכְּבֹדֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And behold — the glory of the Elohim of Israel was coming from the way of the east; and his sound was like the sound of many waters, and the land shone with his glory.

notes.official:
*kəḇôḏ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl bāʾ middereḵ haqqāḏîm* 'the glory of the Elohim of Israel was coming from the way of the east' (`kavod-yhwh`; `elohei-yisrael`). *wəqôlô kəqôl mayim rabbîm* 'and his sound was like the sound of many waters' repeats the simile of 1:24 (`qol-mayim-rabbim`). *qôl* is rendered 'sound' as there (ASV 'his voice'). The suffix may refer to the Elohim of Israel ('his') or to the glory ('its'); the line has 'his'. *wəhāʾāreṣ hēʾîrâ mikkəḇōḏô* 'and the land shone with his glory' (`eretz`; ASV 'the earth').

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east ... like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory') and reads the glory as the large ship of the creators approaching. The line renders *kāḇôḏ* 'glory' under the central entry and keeps the Hebrew simile.

paragraphs.text: וּכְמַרְאֵ֨ה הַמַּרְאֶ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאִ֗יתִי כַּמַּרְאֶ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֙יתִי֙ בְּבֹאִי֙ לְשַׁחֵ֣ת אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וּמַרְא֕וֹת כַּמַּרְאֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי אֶל־נְהַר־כְּבָ֑ר וָאֶפֹּ֖ל אֶל־פָּנָֽי׃

i18n.en: And like the appearance of the vision that I saw — like the vision that I had seen when I came to destroy the city — and visions like the vision that I had seen by the river Kebar; and I fell on my face.

notes.official: *kəmarʾēh hammarʾeh ʾăšer rāʾîṯî* 'like the appearance of the vision that I saw': the stacked appearance formula (`mar'eh-demut`) links three earlier visions. *bəḇōʾî ləšaḥēṯ ʾeṯ-hāʿîr* 'when I came to destroy the city' is the MT, referring to the prophet announcing the destruction (chs. 8-11; cf. 9:1-8). Some Hebrew manuscripts and versions read *bəḇōʾô* 'when he came', and NRSV follows them. The MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *nəhar-kəḇār* 'the river Kebar' (`nehar-kevar`).

paragraphs.text: וּכְב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה בָּ֣א אֶל־הַבָּ֑יִת דֶּ֣רֶךְ שַׁ֔עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּנָ֖יו דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַקָּדִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the glory of YHWH came into the house by the way of the gate whose face was toward the east.

notes.official: *ûḵəḇôḏ YHWH bāʾ ʾel-habbāyiṯ* 'And the glory of YHWH came into the house' (`kavod-yhwh`) by the east gate, reversing the departure of 10:18-19 and 11:22-23.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ וַתְּבִיאֵ֕נִי אֶל־הֶֽחָצֵ֖ר הַפְּנִימִ֑י וְהִנֵּ֛ה מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה הַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: And ruach lifted me up and brought me into the inner court; and behold — the glory of YHWH filled the house.

notes.official: *wattiśśāʾēnî rûaḥ* 'And ruach lifted me up' (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`; ASV 'the Spirit'). *wəhinnēh mālēʾ ḵəḇôḏ-YHWH habbāyiṯ* 'and behold — the glory of YHWH filled the house' (`kavod-yhwh`), as at the dedication of the tabernacle (Ex 40:34-35) and of Solomon's Temple (1 Kgs 8:10-11).

paragraphs.text: וָאֶשְׁמַ֛ע מִדַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י מֵהַבָּ֑יִת וְאִ֕ישׁ הָיָ֥ה עֹמֵ֖ד אֶצְלִֽי׃

i18n.en: I heard one speaking to me from the house, while a man was standing beside me.

notes.official: *wāʾešmaʿ middabbēr ʾēlay mēhabbāyiṯ* 'I heard one speaking to me from the house': *middabbēr* is the Hithpael participle used at 2:2. *wəʾîš hāyâ ʿōmēḏ ʾeṣlî* 'while a man was standing beside me', the measuring man of 40:3.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ אֶת־מְק֣וֹם כִּסְאִ֗י וְאֶת־מְקוֹם֙ כַּפּ֣וֹת רַגְלַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֶשְׁכָּן־שָׁ֛ם בְּת֥וֹךְ בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעוֹלָ֑ם וְלֹ֣א יְטַמְּא֣וּ ע֣וֹד בֵּֽית־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֞י הֵ֤מָּה וּמַלְכֵיהֶם֙ בִּזְנוּתָ֔ם וּבְפִגְרֵ֥י מַלְכֵיהֶ֖ם בָּמוֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, this is the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel forever. And the house of Israel shall no longer defile my holy name — they and their kings — by their whoredom and by the corpses of their kings, their high places,

notes.official:
*ʾeṯ-məqôm kisʾî* 'this is the place of my throne' has no verb; 'this is' is supplied, as the ASV does in brackets. *ʾăšer ʾeškān-šām* 'where I will dwell' (`shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`, whose rationale already cites Ezek 43:7, 9).

*ûḇəp̄iḡrê malḵêhem bāmôṯām* 'and by the corpses of their kings, their high places'. *pəḡārîm* may mean memorial monuments rather than corpses (cf. Lev 26:30). The MT *bāmôṯām* 'their high places' is kept; many read *bəmôṯām* 'at their death', with some manuscripts and Theodotion (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

The speech that opens here has no new speaker until 'He said to me' in v 18; the direct address in v 10 ('As for you, son of human') belongs to it. It is therefore kept open through v 17 (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: בְּתִתָּ֨ם סִפָּ֜ם אֶת־סִפִּ֗י וּמְזֽוּזָתָם֙ אֵ֣צֶל מְזוּזָתִ֔י וְהַקִּ֖יר בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְטִמְּא֣וּ ׀ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֗י בְּתֽוֹעֲבוֹתָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֔וּ וָאֲכַ֥ל אֹתָ֖ם בְּאַפִּֽי׃

i18n.en: when they set their threshold by my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost, with the wall between me and them; and they defiled my holy name by their abominations that they committed, so I consumed them in my anger.

notes.official: *bətittām sippām ʾeṯ-sippî ûməzûzāṯām ʾēṣel məzûzāṯî* 'when they set their threshold by my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost': the palace complex directly adjoined the Temple (1 Kgs 7:1-12), with only a wall between. *bəṯôʿăḇôṯām* 'by their abominations' (`toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword`).

paragraphs.text: עַתָּ֞ה יְרַחֲק֧וּ אֶת־זְנוּתָ֛ם וּפִגְרֵ֥י מַלְכֵיהֶ֖ם מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Now let them put their whoredom and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell in their midst forever.

notes.official: *wəšāḵantî ḇəṯôḵām ləʿôlām* 'and I will dwell in their midst forever' (`shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`), as in v 7.

paragraphs.text: אַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם הַגֵּ֤ד אֶת־בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־הַבַּ֔יִת וְיִכָּלְמ֖וּ מֵעֲוֺנֽוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וּמָדְד֖וּ אֶת־תָּכְנִֽית׃

i18n.en: As for you, son of human, declare the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities; and let them measure the plan.

notes.official: *ûmāḏəḏû ʾeṯ-toḵnîṯ* 'and let them measure the plan'. *toḵnîṯ* is from *tkn* 'measure, regulate', so 'proportion, measured plan' (BDB; HALOT; elsewhere only at 28:12). The ASV 'pattern' would give the same English word as *tabnîṯ* (8:3, 10; 10:8), a different lexeme, so 'plan' is used (`tabnit-toknit-tekhunah-pattern-plan-arrangement-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְאִֽם־נִכְלְמ֞וּ מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֗וּ צוּרַ֣ת הַבַּ֡יִת וּתְכוּנָת֡וֹ וּמוֹצָאָ֡יו וּמוֹבָאָ֣יו וְֽכָל־צֽוּרֹתָ֡ו וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־חֻקֹּתָיו֩ וְכָל־צורתי [צ֨וּרֹתָ֤יו] וְכָל־תורתו [תּוֹרֹתָיו֙] הוֹדַ֣ע אוֹתָ֔ם וּכְתֹ֖ב לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְיִשְׁמְר֞וּ אֶת־כָּל־צוּרָת֛וֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־חֻקֹּתָ֖יו וְעָשׂ֥וּ אוֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And if they are ashamed of all that they have done, make known to them the form of the house and its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, and all its forms, and all its statutes, and all its forms, and all its laws; and write it before their eyes, so that they may keep its whole form and all its statutes, and do them.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, two readings: Ketiv *ṣwrty* / Qere *ṣûrōṯāyw* 'its forms'; Ketiv *twrtw* 'its law' / Qere *tôrōṯāyw* 'its laws' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). *ṣûraṯ habbayiṯ ûṯəḵûnāṯô* 'the form of the house and its arrangement': *təḵûnâ* is from the same root as *toḵnîṯ* in v 10 (`tabnit-toknit-tekhunah-pattern-plan-arrangement-ezekiel`). The MT lists 'all its forms' twice, which the LXX does not; the repetition is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָ֠הָר כָּל־גְּבֻל֞וֹ סָבִ֤יב ׀ סָבִיב֙ קֹ֣דֶשׁ קָדָשִׁ֔ים הִנֵּה־זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: This is the law of the house: on the top of the mountain, its whole territory all around shall be most holy. Behold, this is the law of the house.

notes.official: *zōʾṯ tôraṯ habbāyiṯ* 'This is the law of the house' frames the verse at both ends. *qōḏeš qŏḏāšîm* 'most holy': in Ezekiel the whole mountain-top precinct receives the superlative holiness that Exodus and Kings reserve for the inner sanctuary.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ בָּֽאַמּ֔וֹת אַמָּ֥ה אַמָּ֖ה וָטֹ֑פַח וְחֵ֨יק הָאַמָּ֜ה וְאַמָּה־רֹ֗חַב וּגְבוּלָ֨הּ אֶל־שְׂפָתָ֤הּ סָבִיב֙ זֶ֣רֶת הָאֶחָ֔ד וְזֶ֖ה גַּ֥ב הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

i18n.en: And these are the measurements of the altar by cubits — the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: the bottom, a cubit, and the width, a cubit; and its border on its edge all around, one span. And this is the base of the altar.

notes.official: *bāʾammôṯ ʾammâ ʾammâ wāṭōp̄aḥ* 'by cubits — the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth', the long cubit of 40:5 (`measures-cubit-handbreadth-span-reed-ezekiel`). The altar terms follow the ASV under `altar-structure-terms-heq-gab-gevul-azarah-ezekiel-43`. *ḥêq* 'bottom' (literally 'bosom') is the base or gutter around the foot of the altar. *gəḇûl* 'border' is a rim. *zereṯ* 'span' is half a cubit. *wəzeh gaḇ hammizbēaḥ* 'And this is the base of the altar': *gaḇ* is 'back, raised surface'; NRSV takes it as 'the height of the altar'. The altar is a stepped structure that Albright compared to the Mesopotamian ziggurat (*Archaeology and the Religion of Israel*, 1942).

paragraphs.text: וּמֵחֵ֨יק הָאָ֜רֶץ עַד־הָעֲזָרָ֤ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה֙ שְׁתַּ֣יִם אַמּ֔וֹת וְרֹ֖חַב אַמָּ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת וּמֵהֳעֲזָרָ֨ה הַקְּטַנָּ֜ה עַד־הָעֲזָרָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע אַמּ֔וֹת וְרֹ֖חַב הָאַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And from the bottom on the ground to the lower ledge, two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the greater ledge, four cubits, and the width a cubit.

notes.official: *ûmēḥêq hāʾāreṣ* 'And from the bottom on the ground': *ʾereṣ* is the ground level of the structure. The proposed context clause of `eretz` gives 'ground', as at 42:6. *hāʿăzārâ* 'the ledge': *ʿăzārâ* elsewhere means a court or enclosure (2 Chr 4:9; 6:13). Here it is each of the two receding stages of the altar, lower and upper, called 'smaller' and 'greater' (`altar-structure-terms-heq-gab-gevul-azarah-ezekiel-43`).

paragraphs.text: וְהַֽהַרְאֵ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע אַמּ֑וֹת וּמֵהָאֲרִאֵ֣יל וּלְמַ֔עְלָה הַקְּרָנ֖וֹת אַרְבַּֽע׃

i18n.en: And the altar hearth, four cubits; and from the altar hearth upward, the horns, four.

notes.official: *wəhahar'ēl ʾarbaʿ ʾammôṯ ûmēhāʾăriʾêl ûləmaʿlâ haqqərānôṯ ʾarbaʿ* 'And the altar hearth, four cubits; and from the altar hearth upward, the horns, four'. The topmost block is named in two spellings within the verse, *harʾēl* and *ʾăriʾêl*, and a third (Ketiv/Qere) in v 16. *ʾăriʾēl* is attested in the Mesha inscription (line 12) and as a name for Jerusalem in Isa 29:1-2 ('she shall be to me as an *ʾăriʾēl*'), and is generally taken as 'altar hearth'. *harʾēl* is vocalized as if 'mountain of El' and is usually explained as a variant spelling or reinterpretation of the same word; Albright compared Akkadian *arallû*. The ASV gives two different terms ('upper altar' / 'altar hearth'). The line uses 'altar hearth' for all the spellings, as NRSV does, and records *harʾēl* here (`harel-ariel-altar-hearth-ezekiel-43`). *haqqərānôṯ* 'the horns' (`qarnot-ha-mizbeach-horns-of-the-altar-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: והאראיל [וְהָאֲרִיאֵ֗ל] שְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ בִּשְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה רֹ֑חַב רָב֕וּעַ אֶ֖ל אַרְבַּ֥עַת רְבָעָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And the altar hearth, twelve long by twelve wide, square on its four sides.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *whʾrʾyl* / Qere *wəhāʾărîʾêl* 'and the altar hearth' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; `harel-ariel-altar-hearth-ezekiel-43`). *šətêm ʿeśrēh ʾōreḵ bištêm ʿeśrēh rōḥaḇ* 'twelve long by twelve wide'. The Hebrew gives no unit, and 'cubits' is not supplied, since the English construes without it (ASV '[cubits]' in brackets) (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְהָעֲזָרָ֞ה אַרְבַּ֧ע עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֹ֗רֶךְ בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ רֹ֔חַב אֶ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣עַת רְבָעֶ֑יהָ וְהַגְּבוּל סָבִ֨יב אוֹתָ֜הּ חֲצִ֣י הָאַמָּ֗ה וְהַֽחֵיק־לָ֤הּ אַמָּה֙ סָבִ֔יב וּמַעֲלֹתֵ֖הוּ פְּנ֥וֹת קָדִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the ledge, fourteen long by fourteen wide on its four sides; and the border around it, half a cubit; and its bottom, a cubit all around; and its steps facing east."

notes.official: *wəhāʿăzārâ* 'And the ledge', fourteen by fourteen, again with no unit supplied (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`; `altar-structure-terms-heq-gab-gevul-azarah-ezekiel-43`). *ûmaʿălōṯēhû pənôṯ qāḏîm* 'and its steps facing east'. The covenant code forbids steps up to an altar (Ex 20:26 [MT 20:23]), and Ezekiel's altar has them; commentators note the difference (Zimmerli). The speech of 43:7-17 closes here.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אֵ֚לֶּה חֻקּ֣וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּי֖וֹם הֵעָֽשׂוֹת֑וֹ לְהַעֲל֤וֹת עָלָיו֙ עוֹלָ֔ה וְלִזְרֹ֥ק עָלָ֖יו דָּֽם׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, thus says the Lord YHWH: 'These are the statutes of the altar on the day it is made, for offering burnt-offerings on it and for dashing blood on it.

notes.official: *kōh ʾāmar ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'thus says the Lord YHWH': the oracle runs in single quotes from here to v 27 (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-ezekiel`). *ʾēlleh ḥuqqôṯ hammizbēaḥ* 'These are the statutes of the altar'. *ləhaʿălôṯ ʿālāyw ʿôlâ* 'for offering burnt-offerings on it' (`olah-burnt-offering`). *wəlizrōq ʿālāyw dām* 'and for dashing blood on it': *zāraq* is to throw or toss blood from a basin (*mizrāq*) against the altar. That is a different act from sprinkling (*hizzâ*, Lev 4:6, 17; 16:14), so the ASV 'sprinkle' is replaced by 'dash', as in NRSV and NJPS (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים הַלְוִיִּ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵם֩ מִזֶּ֨רַע צָד֜וֹק הַקְּרֹבִ֣ים אֵלַ֗י נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה לְשָֽׁרְתֵ֑נִי פַּ֥ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֖ר לְחַטָּֽאת׃

i18n.en: You shall give to the priests the Levites who are of the seed of Zadok, who are near to me, declares the Lord YHWH, to minister to me, a young bull for a sin-offering.

notes.official: *hakkōhănîm halləwiyyim ʾăšer hēm mizzeraʿ ṣāḏôq* 'the priests the Levites who are of the seed of Zadok' (cf. 40:46; 44:15). *par ben-bāqār ləḥaṭṭāʾṯ* 'a young bull for a sin-offering' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ מִדָּמ֗וֹ וְנָ֨תַתָּ֜ה עַל־אַרְבַּ֤ע קַרְנֹתָיו֙ וְאֶל־אַרְבַּע֙ פִּנּ֣וֹת הָעֲזָרָ֔ה וְאֶֽל־הַגְּב֖וּל סָבִ֑יב וְחִטֵּאתָ֥ אוֹת֖וֹ וְכִפַּרְתָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And you shall take some of its blood and put it on its four horns and on the four corners of the ledge and on the border all around; thus you shall cleanse it and make atonement for it.

notes.official: *wənāṯattâ ʿal-ʾarbaʿ qarnōṯāyw* 'and put it on its four horns' (`qarnot-ha-mizbeach-horns-of-the-altar-cross-corpus`), *wəʾel-ʾarbaʿ pinnôṯ hāʿăzārâ* 'on the four corners of the ledge' (`altar-structure-terms-heq-gab-gevul-azarah-ezekiel-43`). *wəḥiṭṭēʾṯā ʾôṯô wəḵippartāhû* 'thus you shall cleanse it and make atonement for it'. *ḥiṭṭēʾ* is the Piel 'de-sin, purge', the verb of *ḥaṭṭāʾṯ*; *kippēr* is 'make atonement' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). Both are kept as in the ASV.

paragraphs.text: וְלָ֣קַחְתָּ֔ אֵ֖ת הַפָּ֣ר הַֽחַטָּ֑את וּשְׂרָפוֹ֙ בְּמִפְקַ֣ד הַבַּ֔יִת מִח֖וּץ לַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: And you shall take the bull of the sin-offering, and it shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary.

notes.official: *ûśərāp̄ô bəmip̄qaḏ habbayiṯ miḥûṣ lammiqdāš* 'and it shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary'. The bull of the sin-offering (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`) is burned outside the holy area, as in Lev 4:12, 21 and 16:27. *mip̄qāḏ* is an 'appointed place' (cf. the gate of that name, Neh 3:31).

paragraphs.text: וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּקְרִ֛יב שְׂעִיר־עִזִּ֥ים תָּמִ֖ים לְחַטָּ֑את וְחִטְּאוּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר חִטְּא֖וּ בַּפָּֽר׃

i18n.en: And on the second day you shall offer a male goat without blemish for a sin-offering; and they shall cleanse the altar as they cleansed it with the bull.

notes.official: *śəʿîr-ʿizzîm tāmîm* 'a male goat without blemish' for the second day. *wəḥiṭṭəʾû* 'and they shall cleanse' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: בְּכַלּוֹתְךָ֖ מֵֽחַטֵּ֑א תַּקְרִיב֙ פַּ֣ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֣ר תָּמִ֔ים וְאַ֥יִל מִן־הַצֹּ֖אן תָּמִֽים׃

i18n.en: When you have finished cleansing it, you shall offer a young bull without blemish and a ram from the flock without blemish.

notes.official: *bəḵallôṯəḵā mēḥaṭṭēʾ* 'When you have finished cleansing it' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). *ʾayil min-haṣṣōʾn tāmîm* 'a ram from the flock without blemish': *ʾayil* 'ram' is a homonym of the architectural *ʾayil* 'post' of ch. 40 (`ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: וְהִקְרַבְתָּ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְהִשְׁלִ֨יכוּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים עֲלֵיהֶם֙ מֶ֔לַח וְהֶעֱל֥וּ אוֹתָ֛ם עֹלָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: You shall present them before YHWH, and the priests shall throw salt upon them and offer them up as a burnt-offering to YHWH.

notes.official: *wəhišlîḵû hakkōhănîm ʿălêhem melaḥ* 'and the priests shall throw salt upon them': salt accompanies offerings (Lev 2:13). *wəheʿĕlû ʾôṯām ʿōlâ* 'and offer them up as a burnt-offering' (`olah-burnt-offering`).

paragraphs.text: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה שְׂעִיר־חַטָּ֖את לַיּ֑וֹם וּפַ֧ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֛ר וְאַ֥יִל מִן־הַצֹּ֖אן תְּמִימִ֥ים יַעֲשֽׂוּ׃

i18n.en: Seven days you shall prepare a goat for a sin-offering every day; and a young bull and a ram from the flock, without blemish, they shall prepare.

notes.official: *śəʿîr-ḥaṭṭāʾṯ* 'a goat for a sin-offering' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). *šiḇʿaṯ yāmîm* 'Seven days': the seven-day consecration repeats the ordination of the priests and altar in Ex 29:35-37 and Lev 8:33-35.

paragraphs.text: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים יְכַפְּרוּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְטִֽהֲר֖וּ אֹת֑וֹ וּמִלְא֖וּ ידו [יָדָֽיו׃]

i18n.en: Seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and purify it, and so consecrate it.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *ydw* 'its hand' / Qere *yāḏāyw* 'its hands' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). *ûmilʾû yāḏāyw* is literally 'and they shall fill its hands', the idiom for installing a priest (Ex 28:41; 29:9; Judg 17:5, 12), applied here to the altar. It is rendered by its sense, as in the ASV: 'and so consecrate it' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). *wəṭihărû ʾōṯô* 'and purify it'.

paragraphs.text: וִֽיכַלּ֖וּ אֶת־הַיָּמִ֑ים (ס) וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֜י וָהָ֗לְאָה יַעֲשׂ֨וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ אֶת־עוֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ וְאֶת־שַׁלְמֵיכֶ֔ם וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And when they have completed the days, then on the eighth day and onward the priests shall offer your burnt-offerings and your peace-offerings upon the altar; and I will accept you, declares the Lord YHWH.'"

notes.official: The source has a *setumah* in the middle of the verse, after *wîḵallû ʾeṯ-hayyāmîm* 'and when they have completed the days'. The mark is kept in the Hebrew text, and the English is not broken (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`; cf. 3:16). *ʿôlôṯêḵem wəʾeṯ-šalmêḵem* 'your burnt-offerings and your peace-offerings' (`olah-burnt-offering`; `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). *wəraṣʾṯî ʾeṯḵem* 'and I will accept you'. The oracle and the speech of 43:18-27 close here.
